sections.h2: Selling a house in St. Joseph
sections.html:
A homeowner in St. Joseph has three ways to go: sign with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept an as-is bid from someone paying cash. Let the condition of the house, your deadline and local prices steer the choice.

Prices in St. Joseph run low, with a middle owned-home value of $154,200. At that level, even a few thousand dollars in repairs or fees cuts noticeably into your proceeds. Calculate the net on each route before choosing.

  • Agent sale: broad exposure, with fees and timing tied to the listing contract and the buyer's lender.
  • Owner sale: lower cost, but you do the marketing and the paperwork.
  • Cash sale: the buyer takes the house flaws and all, and you negotiate the closing day.

St. Joseph is the seat of Buchanan County, on the Missouri River about 30 miles north of Kansas City. The mid-2025 population estimate is 71,001, down 2.0% from the 2020 base. Its land area is 44.04 square miles.

The average commute is 17.0 minutes, which helps houses near the center of town.

The St. Joseph School District serves most addresses and runs Benton, Central and Lafayette high schools. A sliver of the city is in Mid-Buchanan County R-V. Check which applies to you, because many families begin a search by district.

Shopping is concentrated along North Belt Highway on the east side, including East Hills Mall, and two interstates, I-29 and I-229, connect the city to Kansas City and Council Bluffs. Plans call for replacing the downtown stretch of I-229 with a surface boulevard, so a house near that corridor deserves a question to the city. St. Joseph Transit runs buses in town, and the nearest airline airport is Kansas City International, about 35 miles south.

St. Joseph runs a Residential Rental Certification Program that began in July 2019 and requires rental units to pass a minimum code inspection every five years. A buyer who intends to keep a rental rented will care whether the house is certified.

The city's application materials list an inspection fee of $50.00 for each inspection by a city inspector, and rentals also need a business license. Forms go to the Housing Compliance Inspection Office, 1100 Frederick Avenue, City Hall Room 107.

  • Business license for rental units: online application.
  • Unit Certification Application and Consent of Entry forms.
  • Residential Rental Unit Inspection Checklist, which shows what inspectors look for on the exterior and interior.
  • Tenant Complaint Form, useful to know about if a tenant has raised concerns.

Before listing or signing a contract, ask Housing Compliance whether your address holds a current certificate. Owners living in the house can phone the same office to learn if any inspection touches the parcel.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Buchanan County
sections.html:
The Buchanan County Recorder of Deeds files St. Joseph deeds. Visit 411 Jules Street, Room 103, St. Joseph, MO 64501, on a weekday between eight in the morning and half past four, or call 816-271-1437. Recording stops at 4:00 p.m. Anything delivered later waits and is recorded in the order received when the office reopens at 8:00 a.m.

Staff there do not prepare deeds or give legal advice, and they point people toward an attorney or title company. Fees vary by document, so call before sending one. Your settlement statement will itemize the recording charge.

A landlord should answer three questions before showing the house. Is the unit certified, and when is the next five-year inspection due? When does the lease end, and what notice does it demand? Would a buyer want the tenant to stay?

Investors look for the lease, rent history and certification papers. Buyers moving in themselves need an empty house and a firm move-out date. Say which one you can deliver so whoever prices the house can plan around it.

If the unit has failed or never had an inspection, the certification program becomes part of the negotiation. One option is to fix the checklist items before listing. The other is to sell as-is, leaving the work to the buyer in return for a lower price and less hassle.

Settle on your own deadline before offers arrive. Note when you need the money, when you plan to move and what the house costs each month in payments, tax and utilities. Together these show what a fast closing is worth.

Speed pays off when monthly costs are high or the house sits empty. Patience pays off when the house is in good shape and you can outwait a buyer's loan. Either is fine if you compare real proceeds.

Buyers in a lower-priced market compare houses closely, so small fixes matter. Mow, clear out the garage, replace dead bulbs and wash the windows. Look at the basement for damp spots and the roof for missing shingles, because those are the items an inspector will put in writing.

If the list of repairs is long, collect two estimates for the biggest items. Then you can tell a cash buyer exactly what the house needs, and you can judge whether their bid is close to what the work really costs.

Keep receipts for any work done in recent years, along with warranties on the roof, furnace or water heater. A folder of paperwork tells buyers the house has been looked after, and it speeds up the title and lender review.

Roys Branch, Whitehead Creek and the Missouri River all touch the city. A house near water should come with an elevation certificate, flood insurance records and repair receipts, if you have them. Learn what neighbors and the city know about drainage trouble ahead of time, so your answers to buyers are accurate.

sections.h2: What to do before accepting an offer
sections.html:
Begin with the occupancy question. With tenants in the house, find the lease and confirm certification with Housing Compliance.

Next, assemble your deed, payoff statement and newest tax bill. Ask for written offers that state a closing date and who pays title and recording costs. Cash deals stay brief: lien search, signing, recording. Buyers with loans add an appraisal and underwriting, and the schedule stretches.

Order the offers by take-home money after repairs, commissions and carrying costs.

faqs.q: How high are home values in St. Joseph?
faqs.a: About $154,200 for a typical owned home, based on 2020 to 2024 estimates. Median gross rent is $898.

faqs.q: Which office handles a deed for a St. Joseph sale?
faqs.a: The Buchanan County Recorder of Deeds, at 411 Jules Street, Room 103, 816-271-1437. A filing that arrives after 4:00 p.m. is recorded the next business day.

faqs.q: Are St. Joseph rental houses inspected?
faqs.a: Yes. The Residential Rental Certification Program, started in July 2019, has each rental unit pass a minimum code inspection every five years. The application shows a $50.00 fee per city inspection.

faqs.q: Which school district covers most of St. Joseph?
faqs.a: The St. Joseph School District, which includes Benton, Central and Lafayette high schools. Mid-Buchanan County R-V serves a small portion.

faqs.q: Can a St. Joseph house in rough shape be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Houses in rough shape sell through a listing, an owner sale or a cash as-is deal. Rentals should have their certification status checked at the Housing Compliance Inspection Office in City Hall.
